stem: During a Solar System lesson in Surat, Gauri says a planet's temperature can be known from its distance from the Sun alone. Which statement best tests her idea?

options.text: She is right: the planet closest to the Sun is always the hottest.
She is not fully right: a thick heat-trapping atmosphere can make a planet hotter than one closer to the Sun.
She is wrong: distance from the Sun has no effect at all on temperature.
She is right: a planet's atmosphere cannot change its temperature.

teacher.key_rationale: Distance from the Sun is a starting expectation, not the only rule; Venus shows that a thick CO2-rich atmosphere can trap heat strongly. A overgeneralises distance; C denies distance entirely; D drops atmospheric heat trapping.
